title: Quick for facts, explained for concepts
statement: Give feedback at once on simple facts, and on concepts explain why an answer is right or wrong.
detail: The delivery platform's learning-science page lists feedback among the force multipliers that work once the foundations are in place: immediate for basic facts, elaborated, explaining why, for concepts. Its principles page carries the same line, and the reading project took both as its bar, so this is a rule adopted from the platform, not a result measured here.
against: Explained feedback still has to be short for young readers: long feedback text was itself counted a failure for Grade 3 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`, line 283), and a lesson lint caps feedback at 60 words, with 40 as the target (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/scripts/lane-tools/op-lint/README.md`, line 15).

evidence.quote: | **Feedback**        | Immediate for basic facts; elaborated (explaining why) for concepts.   |
| **Feedback** | Immediate for basic facts; elaborated (explaining why) for concepts. |
Long feedback text is itself a failure for Grade 3.
feedback must carry a `misconception_id` and be <= 60 words (hard cap); 41-60 words emits a non-blocking warning (40 is the standard's target).
A criterion is the better hint of the two when the child's error is about a kind of thinking rather than a missed fact, because it transfers to the next item and a page reference does not.
